title: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round

learn.hook: Tie a goat to a peg with a 5 m rope and let it graze: the edge of the grass it eats is a perfect circle!
points: A circle is the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance (the radius r) from a fixed point (the centre O).
A chord joins two points of the circle. A chord through the centre is a diameter, and diameter = 2 × radius.
A point P is inside the circle if OP < r, on it if OP = r, and outside if OP > r.
No chord is longer than a diameter: for a chord AB, AB ≤ OA + OB = 2r (triangle inequality), with equality only when AB passes through O.

example.q: A circle has centre O and radius 6 cm. Where are points P, Q, R with OP = 4 cm, OQ = 6 cm, OR = 7.5 cm?
example.answer: P inside, Q on, R outside

learn.reallife: A compass used in geometry works exactly by the definition: the needle is the centre and the pencil stays at a fixed distance.

games.title: Chord facts
items: It joins two points of the circle.
Only chords through the centre are diameters.
A chord of length 13 cm is possible in a circle of radius 6 cm.
The centre is inside the circle.
Its distance from itself is 0 < r.
A radius joins the centre to a point on the circle.

quiz.q: A circle has diameter 18 cm. What is its radius?
quiz.explain: Radius = diameter ÷ 2.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

quiz.q: Which is the longest chord of a circle?
quiz.explain: The diameter passes through the centre and has length 2r, the maximum.
steps: For a chord AB, AB ≤ OA + OB = 2r.
Equality holds only when AB passes through O, i.e. a diameter.
A radius is not a chord.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a radius is a chord

quiz.q: A circle has radius 7 cm. Which chord length is impossible?
quiz.explain: The longest chord is the diameter, 14 cm.
steps: 15 cm > 14 cm, so it is impossible.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that chords cannot exceed the diameter

quiz.q: A circle has centre O and radius 4 cm. OP = 3.5 cm. Where is P?
steps: So P is inside the circle.
quiz.mistake: Compares with the diameter instead of the radius

quiz.q: A goat is tied to a peg with a 6 m rope. Which describes the boundary of the area it can graze?
options: A circle of radius 6 m centred at the peg
quiz.explain: Every point at the end of the tight rope is 6 m from the peg.
steps: With the rope tight, the goat is always 6 m from the peg.
All points 6 m from a fixed point form a circle of radius 6 m.
Answer: A circle of radius 6 m centred at the peg
quiz.mistake: Uses the rope length as the diameter

quiz.q: Why can a chord AB never be longer than 2r?
options: Because AB ≤ OA + OB = r + r
Because chords never pass through O
quiz.explain: In triangle OAB, one side is less than the sum of the other two (or equal if O lies on AB).
steps: In triangle OAB, a side is at most the sum of the other two.
Answer: Because AB ≤ OA + OB = r + r
quiz.mistake: Cannot connect chord length with the triangle inequality

quiz.q: Point Q is 9 cm from the centre of a circle of diameter 18 cm. Where is Q?
quiz.explain: Radius = 9 cm and OQ = 9 cm.
steps: So Q is on the circle.
quiz.mistake: Compares OQ with the diameter

quiz.q: A wheel has spokes from the hub to the rim, each 35 cm. What is the wheel's diameter?
quiz.explain: Spokes are radii; diameter = 2 × 35.
steps: Each spoke runs from the hub (centre) to the rim: a radius of 35 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes the spoke as the diameter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What is a chord, and which chord is the longest?"
teach.praise: Perfect! A chord joins two points on the circle and the diameter through the centre is the longest!
teach.nudge: What does a chord join? Which special chord passes through the centre?

revise.summary: A circle is all points at a fixed distance r from a centre O. A chord joins two points of the circle; the diameter (2r) is the longest chord.
focus: Use diameter = 2 × radius.
Decide if a point is inside, on or outside a circle.
Explain why no chord exceeds the diameter.
remember: Inside: OP < r; on: OP = r; outside: OP > r.
AB ≤ OA + OB = 2r, equal only for a diameter.
r = 6 cm: OP = 4 inside, OQ = 6 on, OR = 7.5 outside.
traps: Compare with the radius, not the diameter.
A radius is not a chord.
Don't double when asked for the radius.

learn.hook: How many different circles can pass through your pencil dot? Infinitely many!
points: Every line through the centre is a line of symmetry of a circle, so a circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry.
A circle also has rotational symmetry about its centre by every angle: turn it by 1°, 37° or 200° and it looks the same.
Through one point, infinitely many circles can be drawn. Through two points A and B, also infinitely many.
The centre of any circle through A and B is equally far from A and B, so it lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
The smallest circle through A and B has AB as its diameter, so its radius is AB/2.

example.q: A and B are 10 cm apart. What is the radius of the smallest circle through both, and where is its centre?
steps: Centre must be on the perpendicular bisector of AB
Closest such point to A is the midpoint M
example.answer: 5 cm, centred at the midpoint of AB

learn.reallife: A wheel can be fitted any way round on its axle because of its rotational symmetry.

games.title: Symmetry check
items: A circle has exactly 4 lines of symmetry.
Every line through the centre works: infinitely many.
A circle looks the same after turning by any angle about its centre.
Only one circle passes through two given points.
Infinitely many do; their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector.
The centre of a circle through A and B is equidistant from A and B.
Both are on the circle, so OA = OB = r.
A line not through the centre can be a line of symmetry of a circle.
Only lines through the centre are.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
quiz.explain: Every line through the centre divides it into two mirror halves.
steps: Every line through the centre divides the circle into mirror halves.
There are infinitely many such lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the horizontal and vertical lines

quiz.q: Which line is a line of symmetry of a circle?
quiz.explain: Folding along any line through the centre makes the halves match.
steps: A line of symmetry must fold the circle onto itself.
Folding along any line through the centre matches the halves.
A chord not through the centre or a tangent does not.
Answer: Any line through its centre
quiz.mistake: Thinks every chord is a line of symmetry

quiz.q: By which angles can a circle be rotated about its centre and still look the same?
quiz.explain: A circle has rotational symmetry for all angles.
steps: Turning a circle about its centre by any angle gives the same circle.
So it has rotational symmetry for every angle.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a circle with a square

quiz.q: How many circles pass through two given points A and B?
quiz.explain: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of AB can be a centre.
steps: A centre O must have OA = OB.
Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB works.
That line has infinitely many points.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two points fix a circle

quiz.q: Where do the centres of all circles through A and B lie?
options: On the perpendicular bisector of AB
quiz.explain: The centre O must satisfy OA = OB.
steps: The centre O satisfies OA = OB.
Points equidistant from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
Answer: On the perpendicular bisector of AB
quiz.mistake: Thinks the centre lies on AB itself

quiz.q: P and Q are 14 cm apart. What is the radius of the smallest circle through both?
quiz.explain: The smallest circle has PQ as diameter.
steps: The smallest circle through P and Q has PQ as diameter.
quiz.mistake: Takes the distance as the radius

quiz.q: A circle through A and B has centre O on the perpendicular bisector, 12 cm from the midpoint M, with AB = 10 cm. What is its radius?
quiz.explain: OA² = OM² + MA² = 144 + 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds the lengths instead of using Pythagoras

quiz.q: Can a circle of radius 4 cm pass through two points 10 cm apart?
options: Yes, if the centre is on AB
No, circles cannot pass through two points
No, the largest possible distance between two points on it is 8 cm
quiz.explain: Two points on a circle are at most a diameter (8 cm) apart.
steps: Two points on a circle are at most a diameter apart.
10 cm > 8 cm, so it is impossible.
Answer: No, the largest possible distance between two points on it is 8 cm
quiz.mistake: Forgets the diameter limit

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Where can the centre be if a circle goes through points A and B?"
teach.praise: Excellent! On the perpendicular bisector of AB, and there are infinitely many such circles!
teach.nudge: How far must the centre be from A and from B? On which line are such points?

revise.summary: A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry for every angle. Infinitely many circles pass through two points; their centres lie on the perpendicular bisector.
focus: Describe the symmetries of a circle.
Locate centres of circles through two points.
Find the smallest circle through two points.
remember: Every line through the centre is a line of symmetry.
Centres of circles through A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
Smallest circle through A, B: diameter AB, radius AB/2.
traps: Not every chord is a line of symmetry.
Two points do not fix a single circle.
Two points on a circle are at most a diameter apart.

learn.hook: Three villages want one water tank equally far from all of them. Where should it go? At the circumcentre!
points: Through three non-collinear points there is exactly one circle: its centre is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet.
Through three collinear points there is no circle: the perpendicular bisectors are parallel and never meet.
This circle is the circumcircle of the triangle, and its centre is the circumcentre.
To construct it, draw the perpendicular bisectors of two sides; their meeting point O is the centre and OA is the radius.
The circumcentre is inside an acute triangle, at the midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle, and outside an obtuse triangle.

example.q: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Where is its circumcentre and what is the circumradius?

learn.reallife: Placing a mobile tower equally far from three towns uses the circumcentre of the triangle formed by them.

games.title: Construct a circumcircle
items: Draw the perpendicular bisector of AB
Draw the perpendicular bisector of BC
Draw the circle with centre O and radius OA

quiz.q: How many circles pass through three non-collinear points?
quiz.explain: The perpendicular bisectors meet at one point, giving one centre and one radius.
steps: Perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet at exactly one point.
That gives one centre and one radius.
quiz.mistake: Confuses three points with two points

quiz.q: How many circles pass through three points on one straight line?
quiz.explain: The perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC are parallel, so there is no common centre.
steps: For collinear points, the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC are parallel.
Parallel lines never meet, so there is no centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks three points always fix a circle

quiz.q: The circumcentre of a triangle is the meeting point of its:
quiz.explain: Each perpendicular bisector holds points equidistant from two vertices.
steps: The circumcentre is equidistant from all three vertices.
Points equidistant from two vertices lie on the perpendicular bisector of that side.
Answer: perpendicular bisectors of the sides
quiz.mistake: Confuses perpendicular bisectors with angle bisectors

quiz.q: Where is the circumcentre of an obtuse triangle?
quiz.explain: For an obtuse triangle the bisectors meet beyond the longest side.
steps: Circumcentre: inside an acute triangle, midpoint of the hypotenuse in a right triangle.
For an obtuse triangle it is outside, beyond the longest side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the centre is always inside

quiz.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse 26 cm. What is its circumradius?
quiz.explain: The hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumcircle.
steps: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is a diameter of the circumcircle.
quiz.mistake: Takes the hypotenuse as the radius

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. What is its circumradius?
quiz.explain: Hypotenuse = √(81 + 144) = 15, radius = 15/2.
quiz.mistake: Halves a leg instead of the hypotenuse

quiz.q: To construct a circumcircle, how many perpendicular bisectors must you draw at least?
quiz.explain: Two bisectors already meet at the centre; the third passes through the same point and is a check.
steps: Two perpendicular bisectors already meet at the centre.
The third passes through the same point and is only a check.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all three are needed

quiz.q: Three wells A, B, C form an acute triangle. A pump equally far from all three is placed at:
quiz.explain: Equal distance from three points means the circumcentre, which is inside for an acute triangle.
steps: Equally far from A, B and C means the circumcentre.
For an acute triangle, the circumcentre is inside.
A midpoint of AB is equidistant from only A and B.
Answer: the circumcentre, inside the triangle
quiz.mistake: Chooses a midpoint, which is only equidistant from two points

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the centre of the circle through the three corners of a triangle?"
teach.praise: Superb! Draw perpendicular bisectors of two sides; where they meet is the centre!
teach.nudge: Which special lines of the sides do you draw? What happens where they meet?

revise.summary: Exactly one circle passes through three non-collinear points; its centre (circumcentre) is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet. No circle passes through three collinear points.
focus: Construct a circumcircle.
Locate the circumcentre for acute, right and obtuse triangles.
Find circumradius of a right triangle.
remember: Circumcentre = meeting point of perpendicular bisectors.
Acute: inside; right: midpoint of hypotenuse; obtuse: outside.
Legs 6 and 8: hypotenuse 10, circumradius 5 cm.
traps: Perpendicular bisectors, not angle bisectors.
Two bisectors are enough to find the centre.
The circumcentre is not always inside.

learn.hook: Cut equal-length chords in a round roti and the slices to the centre all have the same angle!
points: The angle subtended by chord AB at the centre is ∠AOB.
Triangle OAB is isosceles because OA = OB = r, so its base angles are equal.
Theorem: equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre. Proof: if AB = CD, then △OAB ≅ △OCD by SSS (OA = OC, OB = OD, AB = CD), so ∠AOB = ∠COD.
Converse: chords that subtend equal angles at the centre are equal. Proof: △OAB ≅ △OCD by SAS, so AB = CD.

example.q: Chord AB subtends 70° at centre O. Find ∠OAB.

learn.reallife: A bicycle wheel's spokes cut the rim into equal arcs because the central angles are equal.

games.title: Which congruence?
pairs: Equal chords give equal central angles
Equal central angles give equal chords

quiz.q: In a circle with centre O, AB = CD and ∠AOB = 48°. What is ∠COD?
quiz.explain: Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre.
steps: Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the angle

quiz.q: Which congruence rule proves that equal chords subtend equal central angles?
quiz.explain: OA = OC, OB = OD (radii) and AB = CD (given): three sides.
steps: In △OAB and △OCD: OA = OC, OB = OD (radii), AB = CD (given).
Three pairs of equal sides: SSS.
No angle is known at the start, so not SAS.
quiz.mistake: Picks SAS although no angle is known

quiz.q: ∠POQ = ∠ROS at the centre O. What can you say about chords PQ and RS?
quiz.explain: This is the converse: equal central angles give equal chords (by SAS).
steps: Converse: equal angles at the centre give equal chords.
△OPQ ≅ △ORS by SAS (two radii and the included angle).
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal angles make chords parallel

quiz.q: Chord AB subtends 100° at the centre O. What is ∠OAB?
quiz.explain: Triangle OAB is isosceles; base angles = (180 − 100)/2.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90 instead of 180

quiz.q: A chord subtends 60° at the centre of a circle of radius 9 cm. How long is the chord?
quiz.explain: The triangle OAB has a 60° angle between equal sides, so it is equilateral.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the chord must be a diameter

quiz.q: Why is triangle OAB isosceles for any chord AB?
options: OA and OB are both radii
quiz.explain: Any two radii of the same circle are equal.
steps: OA and OB are both radii of the same circle.
Answer: OA and OB are both radii
quiz.mistake: Assumes extra facts about the chord

quiz.q: A regular pentagon's corners lie on a circle. What angle does each side subtend at the centre?
quiz.explain: Five equal chords share 360° equally.
steps: The 5 sides are equal chords, so they share 360° equally.
(108° is the interior angle of the pentagon, not the central angle.)
quiz.mistake: Uses the interior angle of the pentagon

quiz.q: Chords AB and CD subtend 70° and 85° at the centre. Which chord is longer?
quiz.explain: In the same circle, a larger central angle gives a longer chord.
steps: In the same circle, a larger central angle gives a longer chord.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the smaller angle gives the longer chord

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why do equal chords make equal angles at the centre?"
teach.praise: Wonderful! Radii and the equal chords give congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles match!
teach.nudge: Which sides of the two triangles are equal? Which congruence rule fits?

revise.summary: Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre (by SSS), and chords that subtend equal central angles are equal (by SAS).
focus: Use the equal chords–equal angles theorem and its converse.
Use the isosceles triangle OAB.
Find central angles of regular polygons.
remember: △OAB is isosceles since OA = OB.
Chord subtending 70°: base angles (180 − 70)/2 = 55°.
Regular pentagon side: 360° ÷ 5 = 72° at the centre.
traps: Use SSS for the theorem; SAS for the converse.
Subtract from 180°, not 90°.
A bigger central angle gives a longer chord, not a shorter one.

topics.title: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord

learn.hook: Fold a paper circle so a chord's ends meet: the fold goes straight through the centre!
points: Theorem: the line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord (△OAM ≅ △OBM by SSS, and the two angles at M are equal and add to 180°).
Converse: the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord (△OAM ≅ △OBM by RHS).
So the perpendicular bisector of any chord passes through the centre; two such bisectors locate the centre of a circle.
Parallel chords: their perpendiculars from O lie on one line. Find each distance with Pythagoras; the gap between the chords is the difference (same side of O) or the sum (opposite sides).

example.q: In a circle of radius 5 cm, parallel chords AB = 8 cm and CD = 6 cm lie on opposite sides of the centre. How far apart are they?

learn.reallife: Archaeologists find the size of a broken round pot by drawing two chords on a piece and crossing their perpendicular bisectors.

games.title: Perpendicular facts
items: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it.
The perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre.
Every point on it is equidistant from the chord's ends.
A line from the centre to any point of a chord is perpendicular to it.
Only the line to the midpoint is.
Two parallel chords on the same side of O are separated by the sum of their distances from O.
Two perpendicular bisectors of chords meet at the centre.

items.q: Distance of a 24 cm chord from O
Distance of a 10 cm chord from O

quiz.q: OM is drawn from centre O to the midpoint M of chord AB. What is ∠OMA?
quiz.explain: The line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it.
steps: The line from the centre to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle depends on the chord length

quiz.q: Which congruence rule proves that the perpendicular from O bisects chord AB?
quiz.explain: Right angles at M, hypotenuses OA = OB, and common side OM.
steps: Hypotenuses OA = OB (radii); OM is common.
quiz.mistake: Uses SSS before knowing AM = MB

quiz.q: In a circle, the perpendicular from O meets chord PQ at N. If PN = 7 cm, what is PQ?
quiz.explain: N is the midpoint, so PQ = 2 × PN.
steps: The perpendicular from O bisects the chord, so N is the midpoint.
quiz.mistake: Thinks N divides PQ unequally

quiz.q: How can you find the centre of a circle drawn on paper?
options: Draw one diameter and take its end
Fold it in any direction once
Draw two chords and their perpendicular bisectors; they meet at the centre
quiz.explain: Each perpendicular bisector passes through the centre, so two of them pin it down.
steps: The perpendicular bisector of any chord passes through the centre.
Draw two chords and their perpendicular bisectors.
Answer: Draw two chords and their perpendicular bisectors; they meet at the centre
quiz.mistake: Needs to know the centre in advance to draw a diameter

quiz.q: A chord of length 16 cm is 6 cm from the centre. What is the radius?
quiz.explain: Half-chord 8 and distance 6 form a right triangle with the radius.
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole chord instead of half

quiz.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm, parallel chords of 12 cm and 16 cm lie on the same side of the centre. How far apart are they?
quiz.explain: Distances: √(100 − 36) = 8 and √(100 − 64) = 6. Same side: 8 − 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds the distances

quiz.q: For the same two chords on opposite sides of the centre, how far apart are they?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides: 8 + 6.
steps: Distances from O: d₁ = √(100 − 36) = 8 and d₂ = √(100 − 64) = 6.
On opposite sides, add the distances.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the distances

quiz.q: Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle. Their midpoints and the centre:
options: all lie on one straight line
quiz.explain: Both perpendiculars from O to the parallel chords lie along the same line.
steps: The perpendiculars from O to two parallel chords lie on one line.
Each perpendicular passes through its chord's midpoint.
So the centre and both midpoints are collinear.
Answer: all lie on one straight line
quiz.mistake: Thinks the midpoints can be anywhere

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What happens when I drop a perpendicular from the centre onto a chord?"
teach.praise: Exactly! It cuts the chord into two equal halves, proved by RHS!
teach.nudge: Where does the perpendicular meet the chord? What can you say about the two parts?

revise.summary: The line from the centre to a chord's midpoint is perpendicular to it, and the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord. So perpendicular bisectors of chords pass through the centre.
focus: Use the perpendicular–bisector theorems.
Find the centre of a given circle.
Find gaps between parallel chords.
remember: OM ⊥ AB when M is the midpoint (SSS); perpendicular bisects (RHS).
r = 5, chords 8 and 6 on opposite sides: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.
Same side: subtract the distances.
traps: Add distances for opposite sides; subtract for the same side.
Use half the chord in Pythagoras.
The midpoints of parallel chords and the centre are collinear.

topics.title: How far is a chord from the centre?

learn.hook: Chords near the edge of a circle are short; chords near the centre are long. Distance decides length!
points: The distance of a chord from the centre is the length of the perpendicular from O to the chord.
Theorem: equal chords are equidistant from the centre. Converse: chords equidistant from the centre are equal.
A longer chord is closer to the centre; a shorter chord is farther. The diameter (distance 0) is the longest.
The midpoints of all chords of a fixed length are the same distance from O, so they lie on a smaller circle with the same centre (a concentric circle).

example.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm, where do the midpoints of all 12 cm chords lie?
steps: Every midpoint is 8 cm from O
example.answer: On a concentric circle of radius 8 cm

learn.reallife: Cut a round roti with a straight knife: a cut through the middle is the longest, and cuts closer to the edge get shorter and shorter.

games.title: From the centre outwards
games.prompt: Chords of a circle of radius 10 cm, closest to O first

games.title: Distance facts
items: Equal chords are equally far from the centre.
A chord 2 cm from the centre is shorter than one 5 cm from the centre.
The distance of a chord means the shortest distance from O to it.
Midpoints of equal chords lie on a concentric circle.
They are all at the same distance from O.
Two chords 4 cm from the centre can have different lengths.

quiz.q: Two chords AB and CD of a circle are each 6 cm from the centre. AB = 16 cm. What is CD?
quiz.explain: Chords equidistant from the centre are equal.
steps: Chords equidistant from the centre are equal.
Both are 6 cm from O, so CD = AB = 16 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the distance as the chord length

quiz.q: Chord PQ is 3 cm from the centre and chord RS is 7 cm from the centre of the same circle. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: The chord closer to the centre is longer.
steps: A chord closer to the centre is longer.
PQ is 3 cm away, RS is 7 cm away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a larger distance means a longer chord

quiz.q: What is the distance of a diameter from the centre?
quiz.explain: A diameter passes through the centre.
steps: A diameter passes through the centre.
Its distance from the centre is 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks distance is measured to an end point

quiz.q: How is the distance of a chord from the centre measured?
options: From the centre to an end of the chord
From the chord to the circle
Along the perpendicular from the centre to the chord
quiz.explain: The perpendicular gives the shortest distance.
steps: Distance from the centre to a chord is the shortest distance.
The shortest distance is along the perpendicular from O to the chord.
Answer: Along the perpendicular from the centre to the chord
quiz.mistake: Measures to an end point, which gives the radius

quiz.q: In a circle of radius 13 cm, the midpoints of all chords of length 10 cm lie on a circle of radius:
quiz.mistake: Uses the half-chord as the radius

quiz.q: Chords AB = 10 cm and CD = 14 cm are in the same circle. Which is nearer to the centre?
quiz.explain: The longer chord is nearer to the centre.
steps: The longer chord is nearer the centre.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the length-distance relation

quiz.q: Which congruence rule proves that equal chords are equidistant from the centre?
quiz.explain: Right angles at the feet of the perpendiculars, equal radii (hypotenuses) and equal half-chords.
steps: Right angles at the feet of the perpendiculars.
Hypotenuses are equal radii; half-chords are equal.
quiz.mistake: Uses SSS without knowing the distances

quiz.q: In a circle of radius 5 cm, the midpoint of a chord is 4 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
quiz.explain: Half-chord = √(25 − 16) = 3, so the chord is 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the half-chord

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How is a chord's distance from the centre related to its length?"
teach.praise: Lovely! Equal chords are equally far, and longer chords are closer to the centre!
teach.nudge: Do equal chords sit at equal distances? Is a longer chord closer or farther?

revise.summary: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, and chords equidistant from the centre are equal. Longer chords are closer to the centre.
focus: Compare chords by their distances from the centre.
Find the distance or length of a chord.
Locate midpoints of equal chords.
remember: Distance = perpendicular from O to the chord.
Diameter: distance 0, the longest chord.
r = 10, chords of 12 cm: midpoints on a concentric circle of radius 8 cm.
traps: A larger distance means a shorter chord.
Distance is not measured to an end point.
Double the half-chord at the end.

learn.hook: Radius, chord, distance: know any two and Baudhayana's theorem gives the third!
points: The radius, the half-chord and the distance d form a right triangle, so r² = (half-chord)² + d².
Chord length = 2√(r² − d²).
Distance d = √(r² − (chord/2)²) and radius r = √((chord/2)² + d²).
Through a point P inside a circle, the shortest chord is the one perpendicular to OP; its length is 2√(r² − OP²). The longest chord through P is the diameter.

example.q: A circle has radius 17 cm. Find the length of a chord 8 cm from the centre.

learn.reallife: A well-digger measuring the width of a round well at a fixed distance from the centre is using this formula.

quiz.q: A circle has radius 13 cm and a chord is 12 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double

quiz.q: A 48 cm chord is drawn in a circle of radius 25 cm. How far is it from the centre?
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole chord 48 in Pythagoras

quiz.q: A chord of length 30 cm is 8 cm from the centre. What is the radius?
quiz.mistake: Adds the half-chord and distance

quiz.q: P is a point 6 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 10 cm. What is the length of the shortest chord through P?
quiz.explain: The shortest chord is perpendicular to OP: 2√(100 − 36) = 2 × 8.
steps: The shortest chord through P is perpendicular to OP.
quiz.mistake: Gives the diameter, which is the longest chord

quiz.q: For the same point P, what is the longest chord through it?
quiz.explain: The longest chord through any point is the diameter, 2 × 10.
steps: The longest chord through any point is a diameter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the perpendicular chord is the longest

quiz.q: The shortest chord through an interior point P is:
options: parallel to a diameter through P only if P = O
quiz.explain: It is the chord farthest from O, and that is the one perpendicular to OP.
steps: A chord farther from O is shorter.
Of all chords through P, the one perpendicular to OP is farthest from O (distance OP).
Answer: perpendicular to the line OP
quiz.mistake: Confuses the shortest chord with the diameter

quiz.q: A round table top has radius 60 cm. A straight wooden strip is fixed 36 cm from its centre. How long is the strip, end to end?
quiz.mistake: Stops at the half-length

quiz.q: A chord 8 cm long is 3 cm from the centre. Another chord in the same circle is 4 cm from the centre. How long is it?
quiz.explain: Radius = √(16 + 9) = 5. Second chord = 2√(25 − 16) = 6.
steps: Half of the 8 cm chord = 4 cm, and it is 3 cm from the centre.
Half of the second chord = √(5² − 4²) = √9 = 3 cm
quiz.mistake: Assumes all chords are the same length

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I find the length of a chord if I know the radius and its distance from the centre?"
teach.praise: Superb! Use the right triangle: half-chord = √(r² − d²), then double it!
teach.nudge: Which right triangle can you draw? What do you do after finding half the chord?

revise.summary: The radius, half-chord and distance from the centre form a right triangle: r² = (half-chord)² + d². The shortest chord through an interior point P is perpendicular to OP.
focus: Find chord length, distance or radius.
Find the shortest and longest chords through a point.
Use Pythagoras with half-chords.
remember: Chord = 2√(r² − d²).
r = 17, d = 8: chord 30 cm.
Shortest chord through P: 2√(r² − OP²); longest: the diameter.
traps: Use half the chord, not the whole chord, in Pythagoras.
Don't stop at the half-length.
The perpendicular chord is the shortest, not the longest.

topics.title: Arcs and the angle at the centre

learn.hook: Two goalposts stand on the edge of a round ground. Seen from the centre, the angle between them is exactly twice the angle seen from any point on the far edge!
points: Two points on a circle split it into two arcs: the smaller is the minor arc, the larger the major arc. If the points are ends of a diameter, both arcs are semicircles.
An arc AB subtends ∠AOB at the centre and ∠APB at a point P on the remaining part of the circle (an inscribed angle).
Theorem: the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle: ∠AOB = 2∠APB.
Proof idea: join PO and extend it. Triangles OAP and OBP are isosceles, so each outer angle at O equals twice the matching base angle; adding gives ∠AOB = 2∠APB.

example.q: Arc AB subtends 130° at the centre. Find the angle it subtends at a point P on the major arc.

learn.reallife: Architects designing arched gates use the doubling rule to set angles of the arch from its centre.

quiz.q: Arc AB subtends 110° at the centre O. What angle does it subtend at a point C on the major arc?
quiz.explain: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre.
steps: Angle at circumference = ½ × angle at centre.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

quiz.q: An inscribed angle ∠PQR is 42°. What is the angle subtended by arc PR at the centre?
quiz.explain: Centre angle = 2 × 42°.
steps: Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference.
quiz.mistake: Halves instead of doubling

quiz.q: Two points on a circle make a minor arc of 140°. What is the major arc?
quiz.explain: The two arcs add to 360°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180°

quiz.q: Which arc is a semicircle?
options: An arc whose ends are the ends of a diameter
quiz.explain: A diameter splits a circle into two equal arcs of 180°.
steps: A diameter splits a circle into two equal arcs.
Answer: An arc whose ends are the ends of a diameter
quiz.mistake: Thinks any large arc is a semicircle

quiz.q: O is the centre and ∠AOB = 2x. A point P on the major arc gives ∠APB = 35°. What is x?
quiz.mistake: Sets 2x = 35

quiz.q: In the proof of 'angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference', why are triangles OAP and OBP isosceles?
options: OA, OB and OP are all radii
quiz.explain: Each triangle has two sides that are radii.
steps: O is the centre; A, B, P are on the circle.
So △OAP and △OBP each have two equal sides.
Answer: OA, OB and OP are all radii
quiz.mistake: Assumes the chord lengths are equal

quiz.q: Arc AB subtends 72° at P on the circle. What is the reflex angle AOB at the centre?
quiz.explain: ∠AOB = 144°, so the reflex angle = 360° − 144°.
quiz.mistake: Gives the non-reflex angle

quiz.q: A chord AB subtends 90° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the major arc?
quiz.explain: Half of 90°.
steps: Angle at the major arc = ½ × angle at centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle stays the same

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How is the angle at the centre related to the angle at the edge for the same arc?"
teach.praise: Yes! The centre angle is double the angle at the circumference!
teach.nudge: Which one is bigger, the angle at the centre or at the edge? By how much?

revise.summary: Two points split a circle into a minor and a major arc. The angle an arc subtends at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
focus: Use ∠AOB = 2∠APB.
Find major and minor arcs.
Follow the isosceles-triangle proof.
remember: Minor + major arc = 360°.
130° at the centre → 65° at the circumference.
Ends of a diameter make two semicircles.
traps: Halve for the circumference angle; don't double.
A large arc is not automatically a semicircle.
Don't subtract from 180° by mistake.

topics.title: Same segment, semicircle and concyclic points

learn.hook: Two lamps stand on the edge of a round pond. Walk along the far side of the edge and the angle between the lamps, as you see them, never changes!
points: Angles in the same segment are equal: all angles subtended by arc AB at points on the same arc are equal (each is half of ∠AOB).
The angle in a semicircle is a right angle: if AB is a diameter, ∠AOB = 180°, so ∠APB = 90° for any point P on the circle.
Points are concyclic if they all lie on one circle.
If a segment AB subtends equal angles at two points C and D on the same side of AB, then A, B, C, D are concyclic.

example.q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is on the circle with ∠CAB = 35°. Find ∠CBA.

learn.reallife: A photographer standing anywhere on a circle through two ends of a stage sees the stage at the same angle.

games.title: Segment facts
items: Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
Each is half the angle at the centre.
The angle in a semicircle is 180°.
It is 90°; the angle at the centre is 180°.
Four corners of a rectangle are concyclic.
The diagonals are diameters of a common circle.
If ∠ACB = ∠ADB with C, D on the same side of AB, then A, B, C, D are concyclic.
Three points fix a circle; the fourth may not lie on it.

quiz.q: C and D are on the same arc of a circle with chord AB. ∠ACB = 38°. What is ∠ADB?
quiz.explain: Angles in the same segment are equal.
steps: C and D lie on the same arc (same segment).
Angles in the same segment are equal.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the angle as if D were the centre

quiz.q: AB is a diameter and P is any point on the circle. What is ∠APB?
quiz.explain: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the angle at the centre

quiz.q: AB is a diameter and C is on the circle with ∠ABC = 27°. What is ∠BAC?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the right angle at C

quiz.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse 20 cm. A circle is drawn with the hypotenuse as diameter. Where is the right-angle vertex?
quiz.explain: Converse of the semicircle theorem: the right-angle vertex lies on the circle with the hypotenuse as diameter.
steps: A right angle subtended by the hypotenuse puts the vertex on the circle with the hypotenuse as diameter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the vertex is inside

quiz.q: What does 'concyclic points' mean?
options: Points that all lie on one circle
Points at equal distances from each other
quiz.explain: Concyclic: on the same circle.
steps: Concyclic means lying on one circle.
Collinear means lying on one line.
Answer: Points that all lie on one circle
quiz.mistake: Confuses concyclic with collinear

quiz.q: Segment PQ subtends ∠PRQ = 50° and ∠PSQ = 50°, with R and S on the same side of PQ. What can you say?
options: P, Q, R, S are concyclic
quiz.explain: Equal angles subtended on the same side imply the four points lie on one circle.
steps: PQ subtends equal angles (50°) at R and S.
R and S are on the same side of PQ.
So P, Q, R, S lie on one circle.
Answer: P, Q, R, S are concyclic
quiz.mistake: Does not know the concyclicity condition

quiz.q: In a circle, ∠AOB = 140° at the centre. Points C and D are on the major arc. What is ∠ACB + ∠ADB?
quiz.explain: Each is 70°, so the sum is 140°.
quiz.mistake: Gives just one of the two angles

quiz.q: Ravi wants to check if four lamp posts are on one circle. Two posts A, B and the others C, D on one side: ∠ACB = 44°, ∠ADB = 47°. Are they concyclic?
options: No, the angles subtended by AB are not equal
quiz.explain: For concyclic points on the same side the angles must be exactly equal.
steps: So the four posts are not on one circle.
Answer: No, the angles subtended by AB are not equal
quiz.mistake: Treats nearly equal angles as equal

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What is the angle in a semicircle and why?"
teach.praise: Brilliant! The diameter makes 180° at the centre, so half of it, 90°, at the edge!
teach.nudge: What angle does a diameter make at the centre? What is half of that?

revise.summary: Angles in the same segment are equal, and the angle in a semicircle is 90°. If a segment subtends equal angles at two points on the same side, the four points are concyclic.
focus: Use angles in the same segment.
Use the angle in a semicircle.
Test four points for concyclicity.
remember: Angle in a semicircle = 90°.
AB diameter, ∠CAB = 35° → ∠CBA = 55°.
Concyclic = on one circle.
traps: Angles in the same segment are equal, not doubled.
Nearly equal angles do not prove concyclicity.
Concyclic is not collinear.

learn.hook: Put the four corners of any four-sided figure on a circle, and its opposite angles always team up to make 180°!
points: A cyclic quadrilateral has all four vertices on a circle.
Theorem: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°. (The two angles stand on arcs that together make the whole circle, so their centre angles add to 360°.)
Converse: if a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral add to 180°, the quadrilateral is cyclic.
An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle.
With algebra: if opposite angles are (2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)°, then 5x + 5 = 180, so x = 35.

example.q: ABCD is cyclic with ∠A = 75° and ∠B = 110°. Find ∠C and ∠D.

learn.reallife: Window frames built in round arches often form cyclic quadrilaterals, so carpenters use the 180° rule.

quiz.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = 68°. What is ∠C?
quiz.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.
steps: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks opposite angles are equal

quiz.q: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, ∠Q = 3∠S. What is ∠S?
quiz.mistake: Uses 360° instead of 180°

quiz.q: Side BC of cyclic quadrilateral ABCD is extended to E. ∠DCE = 84°. What is ∠A?
quiz.explain: The exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.
steps: An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle.
∠DCE is exterior at C; the interior opposite angle is ∠A.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° once more

quiz.q: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are (2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)°. What is x?
quiz.mistake: Sets the angles equal

quiz.q: For x = 35 in the question above, what is the larger of the two angles?
quiz.mistake: Gives the smaller angle

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has ∠A = 95°, ∠B = 70°, ∠C = 85°. Is it cyclic?
options: Yes, all angles are less than 100°
quiz.explain: By the converse, one pair of opposite angles adding to 180° is enough.
steps: By the converse, one opposite pair adding to 180° makes it cyclic.
quiz.mistake: Adds adjacent angles instead of opposite ones

quiz.q: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 80° and ∠B = 105°. What is ∠D?
quiz.explain: ∠D is opposite ∠B: 180° − 105°.
quiz.mistake: Pairs adjacent angles

quiz.q: ABCD is cyclic with diagonal AC. In triangle ABC, ∠BAC = 30° and ∠BCA = 50°. What is ∠ADC?
quiz.explain: ∠ABC = 180° − 30° − 50° = 100°, and ∠ADC is opposite ∠ABC, so it is 180° − 100°.
quiz.mistake: Stops at ∠ABC

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "What's special about the angles of a quadrilateral drawn inside a circle?"
teach.praise: Fantastic! Opposite angles add to 180°, and the exterior angle equals the interior opposite one!
teach.nudge: Which pairs of angles should you look at? What do they add up to?

revise.summary: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°, and the converse is true. An exterior angle equals the interior opposite angle.
focus: Find missing angles of cyclic quadrilaterals.
Test if a quadrilateral is cyclic.
Solve angle equations with algebra.
traps: Opposite angles are supplementary, not equal.
Pair opposite angles, not adjacent ones.
Use 180°, not 360°, for one pair.

learn.hook: Brahmagupta found the area of any four-sided figure on a circle using only its sides, 1400 years ago!
points: A parallelogram is cyclic only if it is a rectangle: opposite angles are equal and must add to 180°, so each is 90°.
The diagonals of a rectangle inscribed in a circle are diameters, so they meet at the centre.
Brahmagupta's formula: a cyclic quadrilateral with sides a, b, c, d and semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c + d)/2 has area √((s − a)(s − b)(s − c)(s − d)).
A regular hexagon in a circle of radius r splits into 6 equilateral triangles, so each side equals r.
The apothem (distance from the centre to a side) of that hexagon is (√3/2)r, the height of an equilateral triangle of side r.

example.q: A cyclic quadrilateral has sides 7, 15, 20 and 24 cm. Find its area.

learn.reallife: Honeycomb cells and many nut-bolt heads are regular hexagons whose side equals the radius of the circle around them.

games.title: Shape check
items: A rhombus that is not a square can be cyclic.
Its opposite angles are equal but not 90°, so they cannot add to 180°.
The side of a regular hexagon in a circle of radius 6 cm is 6 cm.
It is made of equilateral triangles of side r.
The diagonals of an inscribed rectangle meet at the centre of the circle.
Brahmagupta's formula works for every quadrilateral.

quiz.q: Which parallelogram can be inscribed in a circle?
quiz.explain: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal; for a cyclic one they must also add to 180°, so each is 90°.
steps: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
Cyclic needs them to add to 180°, so each is 90°.
A parallelogram with 90° angles is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any parallelogram can be cyclic

quiz.q: A rectangle of sides 12 cm and 5 cm is inscribed in a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
quiz.explain: The diagonal is a diameter: √(144 + 25) = 13, so r = 6.5.
quiz.mistake: Gives the diameter as the radius

quiz.q: Where do the diagonals of a rectangle inscribed in a circle meet?
options: At the centre of the circle
quiz.explain: Each diagonal subtends 90° at the vertices, so it is a diameter; diameters meet at the centre.
steps: Each diagonal subtends 90° at a vertex on the circle.
So each diagonal is a diameter.
Answer: At the centre of the circle
quiz.mistake: Thinks diagonals meet at a random point

quiz.q: Use Brahmagupta's formula for a cyclic quadrilateral with sides 6, 6, 6, 6 cm (a square). What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the square root

quiz.q: A kite has sides 5, 12, 12 and 5 cm with right angles at the two corners where a 5 cm and a 12 cm side meet, so it is cyclic. Using Brahmagupta's formula (s = 17), what is its area?
quiz.mistake: Uses the perimeter instead of the semi-perimeter

quiz.q: A regular hexagon is drawn inside a circle of radius 10 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Each side equals the radius, 10 cm, and there are 6 sides.
steps: Each side of the inscribed regular hexagon = radius = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes the side as the diameter

quiz.q: What is the apothem of a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle of radius 8 cm?
steps: Apothem = height of an equilateral triangle of side r = (√3/2)r.
quiz.mistake: Uses half the radius

quiz.q: Why is each side of a regular hexagon in a circle equal to the radius?
options: Because the hexagon touches the circle
The 6 central angles are 60°, making 6 equilateral triangles
quiz.explain: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°; an isosceles triangle with a 60° apex is equilateral.
steps: Each triangle has two radii as sides and a 60° apex.
Its base angles are (180° − 60°)/2 = 60°, so it is equilateral: side = r.
Answer: The 6 central angles are 60°, making 6 equilateral triangles
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the central angle to equilateral triangles

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why can't a slanted parallelogram fit inside a circle with all corners on it?"
teach.praise: Exactly! Opposite angles must be equal and add to 180°, so they are right angles: a rectangle!
teach.nudge: What must opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to? What about in a parallelogram?

revise.summary: A cyclic parallelogram must be a rectangle, whose diagonals are diameters. Brahmagupta's formula gives the area of a cyclic quadrilateral; a regular hexagon in a circle has side equal to the radius.
focus: Use Brahmagupta's formula.
Explain why a cyclic parallelogram is a rectangle.
Find side and apothem of an inscribed hexagon.
remember: Area = √((s − a)(s − b)(s − c)(s − d)), s = semi-perimeter.
Sides 7, 15, 20, 24: s = 33, area 234 cm².
Hexagon in radius r: side r, apothem (√3/2)r.
traps: Use the semi-perimeter, not the perimeter.
Don't forget the square root.
Not every parallelogram is cyclic.

learn.hook: A giant wheel at the Dussehra mela lifts you up, brings you down, and does it again and again. Things that repeat like this are called periodic!
points: A motion is periodic if it repeats itself exactly after a fixed interval of time.
The time for one complete cycle is the period. The number of cycles in one unit of time is the frequency: frequency = 1 ÷ period.
Examples: the swing of a pendulum, the hands of a clock, a giant wheel, days of the week, phases of the Moon.
To find where a periodic motion is after a long time, divide the time by the period and look at the remainder.
The graph of height against time for a seat on a giant wheel is a smooth wave that rises and falls again and again.

example.q: A giant wheel takes 4 minutes for one full turn. Riya's seat is at the bottom at time 0. Where is it after 22 minutes?
steps: After 5 full turns the seat is back at the bottom
2 minutes is half of a turn, so the seat goes from the bottom to the top
example.answer: At the very top of the wheel

learn.reallife: Your heartbeat, the seasons and the tides all follow repeating cycles. Doctors even count heartbeats per minute, which is a frequency!

games.title: Does it repeat?
items: A ball rolling down a slope and stopping
Height of a rocket after launch

items.q: Pendulum: 30 swings in 60 seconds. Period in seconds?
A wheel turns once in 5 minutes. Turns in 1 hour?
Degrees turned by the minute hand in 20 minutes
Degrees turned by the hour hand in 1 hour
Full turns of the seconds hand in 5 minutes

quiz.q: Which of these is a periodic motion?
options: A leaf falling from a tree
quiz.explain: A pendulum repeats the same back-and-forth swing in equal intervals of time.
steps: Periodic motion repeats exactly after a fixed interval.
A falling leaf, melting ice and a rocket happen once.
A pendulum repeats its swing again and again.
Answer: The swinging of a pendulum
quiz.mistake: Thinks any motion is periodic, even one that happens only once

quiz.q: A pendulum completes 20 swings in 40 seconds. What is its period?
quiz.explain: Period = time for one swing = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 seconds.
steps: Period = total time ÷ number of swings
quiz.mistake: Divides the swings by the time, which gives the frequency (0.5) instead

quiz.q: A fan blade completes one turn every 0.25 seconds. How many turns does it make in one second?
quiz.explain: Frequency = 1 ÷ period = 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 turns per second.
quiz.mistake: Thinks frequency and period are the same number

quiz.q: A giant wheel takes 6 minutes per turn. Kabir's seat starts at the bottom. Where is it after 33 minutes?
options: A quarter of the way round
quiz.explain: 33 = 5 × 6 + 3. After 5 full turns he is back at the bottom; 3 more minutes is half a turn, which takes him to the top.
steps: Half a turn from the bottom = the top
quiz.mistake: Ignores the remainder and thinks he is back at the start

quiz.q: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 25 minutes?
quiz.explain: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, which is 6° per minute. 25 × 6° = 150°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 5° per minute, as if a full turn were 300°

quiz.q: Starting at 12:00, through how many degrees has the hour hand turned at 3:00?
quiz.explain: The hour hand turns 360° in 12 hours, which is 30° per hour. In 3 hours it turns 90°.
quiz.mistake: Gives the angle for only one hour

quiz.q: Today is Monday. What day of the week will it be 100 days from today?
quiz.explain: The days of the week repeat with period 7. 100 = 14 × 7 + 2, so it is 2 days after Monday.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to use the remainder, or counts today as day 1

quiz.q: Harpreet records the height of her seat on a giant wheel every few seconds and draws a graph of height against time. What shape does it have?
options: A single hill and then flat
A wave that rises and falls again and again
quiz.explain: The seat goes up and down in every turn, so the graph repeats the same up-and-down shape each period.
steps: In each turn the seat goes up and then down.
So the height–time graph is a repeating wave.
Answer: A wave that rises and falls again and again
quiz.mistake: Thinks height keeps increasing because the wheel keeps moving

teach.ask: Gappu is dizzy from the giant wheel: "What does it mean when you say the wheel's motion is periodic?"
teach.praise: It repeats the same cycle after the same fixed time, called the period. And frequency tells how many cycles in each second. Wheee!
teach.nudge: Does the wheel take the same time for every round? What do we call that time?

revise.summary: A periodic motion repeats exactly after a fixed time, the period; frequency = 1 ÷ period. Use the remainder after dividing by the period to find the position later.
focus: Identify periodic motions.
Find period and frequency.
Find the position after a long time using remainders.
remember: Frequency = 1 ÷ period.
Wheel: 4 min per turn; 22 min = 5 turns + 2 min → at the top.
Height of a giant-wheel seat vs time: a repeating wave.
traps: A one-time motion is not periodic.
Period and frequency are not the same number.
Don't ignore the remainder.

learn.hook: Every spoke of a cycle wheel sweeps out angles as it turns. One full turn is 360°, but a wheel can keep turning through 720°, 1080° and beyond!
points: A full turn is 360°, a half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°.
Angles are classified as acute (less than 90°), right (90°), obtuse (between 90° and 180°), straight (180°) and reflex (between 180° and 360°).
An angle at the centre of a circle is called a central angle. Equal slices of a circle have equal central angles: n equal slices have 360° ÷ n each.
Arc length for a central angle θ is (θ/360) × 2πr, the same fraction of the full circumference.
Turning anticlockwise is usually taken as positive. Turning through more than 360° just means extra full turns: 450° = 360° + 90°.

example.q: A wheel of radius 35 cm turns through 72°. How far does a point on the rim travel? (Use π = 22/7.)

learn.reallife: A pizza or a birthday cake cut into 8 equal slices gives each slice a central angle of 45°.

quiz.q: A wheel turns through 3/4 of a full turn. What angle is that?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 for a full turn, as with percentages, giving 75°

quiz.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4:00?
quiz.explain: The hour hand is on 4 and the minute hand on 12. Each hour mark is 30° apart, so 4 × 30° = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 25° per hour mark, or gives the larger reflex angle 240°

quiz.q: What type of angle is 135°?
quiz.explain: 135° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any angle over 90° is reflex

quiz.q: A spinning top turns through 900°. How can you describe this turn?
options: 2 full turns and a half turn
2 full turns and a quarter turn
quiz.explain: 900° = 2 × 360° + 180°, which is 2 full turns plus a half turn.
steps: Answer: 2 full turns and a half turn
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 360

quiz.q: In a circle of radius 14 cm, find the length of the arc with a central angle of 90°. (Use π = 22/7.)
quiz.explain: 90° is a quarter of the circle, so the arc is a quarter of the circumference 88 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses a half instead of a quarter, or forgets to take the fraction at all

quiz.q: Joseph cuts a round cake into 8 equal slices from the centre. What is the angle of each slice at the centre?
quiz.explain: The full angle at the centre is 360°, shared equally among 8 slices: 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.
quiz.mistake: Shares 320° or 480° instead of 360°, or confuses the slice count with the angle

quiz.q: An angle of 110° is marked at a point. What is the reflex angle at that point?
quiz.explain: The angles all the way round a point add to 360°, so the reflex angle is 360° − 110° = 250°.
steps: Angles round a point add to 360°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180°, which gives the supplement instead

quiz.q: Aisha's bicycle wheel makes 5 complete turns. Through what total angle has a spoke turned?
quiz.explain: Each full turn is 360°, so 5 turns is 5 × 360° = 1800°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles stop at 360°

teach.ask: Gappu spins round and round: "If I turn all the way round twice, is my angle still 360°?"
teach.praise: One full turn is 360°, so two turns are 720°. And angles can be acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex. My head is spinning, but I get it!
teach.nudge: How many degrees are in one full turn? What happens when you keep turning?

revise.summary: A full turn is 360°. Angles are acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex. Central angles of n equal slices are 360° ÷ n, and arc length is (θ/360) × 2πr.
focus: Classify angles.
Find central angles and reflex angles.
Find arc lengths.
remember: Acute < 90°, obtuse 90°–180°, reflex 180°–360°.
Arc = (θ/360) × 2πr; radius 35, 72° → 44 cm.
traps: A full turn is 360°, not 100.
Reflex = 360° − angle, not 180° − angle.
Not every angle over 90° is reflex.

learn.hook: How high is your seat on the giant wheel right now? With an angle and the radius, trigonometry can tell you without a measuring tape!
points: In a right triangle, for an acute angle θ: the hypotenuse is the longest side, the opposite side is across from θ, and the adjacent side is next to θ.
sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
For a fixed angle these ratios stay the same however big the triangle is, because all such triangles are similar.
A point on a circle of radius r, at angle θ above the horizontal line through the centre, is r sin θ above the centre and r cos θ across from it. Also sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

example.q: A giant wheel has radius 10 m and its centre is 12 m above the ground. Riya's seat is at 30° above the horizontal line through the centre. How high is she?
steps: Height above the centre = r sin θ = 10 × sin 30°

learn.reallife: Engineers use sine and cosine to design ramps, roofs and giant wheels, and to work out heights of towers they cannot climb.

games.title: Trig true or false
items: For an acute angle in a right triangle, sin θ is never more than 1
The opposite side is always shorter than the hypotenuse, so the ratio is less than 1.
In a bigger triangle with the same angles, sin θ is bigger
All sides grow in the same ratio, so the ratio opposite ÷ hypotenuse stays the same.
In a 30°-60°-90° triangle the side next to 60° is half the hypotenuse.
That is sin θ. tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
This comes from Pythagoras: opposite² + adjacent² = hypotenuse².
sin 30° + sin 30° = 1, but sin 60° = √3/2 ≈ 0.87. You cannot add angles inside sin like that.

quiz.q: A right triangle has sides 3, 4 and 5. For the angle θ opposite the side 3, what is sin θ?
quiz.explain: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 3 ÷ 5.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the adjacent side, which gives tan θ

quiz.q: In the same 3-4-5 triangle, what is tan θ for the angle opposite the side 3?
quiz.explain: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 3 ÷ 4.
quiz.mistake: Turns the ratio upside down

quiz.q: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall, making 30° with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach?
quiz.explain: The height is opposite the 30° angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse. Height = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 1/2 = 5 m.
quiz.mistake: Uses cos 30° (giving 8.66 m), which is the distance along the ground

quiz.q: What is the value of sin 30°?
quiz.explain: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle the side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse, so sin 30° = 1/2.
steps: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sin 30° with sin 60° = √3/2

quiz.q: A giant wheel of radius 8 m has its centre 10 m above the ground. A seat is 30° below the horizontal line through the centre. How high is the seat?
quiz.explain: The seat is 8 × sin 30° = 4 m below the centre, so its height is 10 − 4 = 6 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 4 m even though the seat is below the centre

quiz.q: θ is an acute angle with sin θ = 5/13. What is cos θ?
quiz.explain: Draw a right triangle with opposite 5 and hypotenuse 13. The adjacent side is √(169 − 25) = 12, so cos θ = 12/13.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 5 from 13 to get the adjacent side as 8

quiz.q: As θ increases from 0° to 90°, what happens to sin θ?
quiz.explain: sin 0° = 0 and sin 90° = 1. As the angle opens up, the opposite side grows compared with the hypotenuse.
steps: As θ grows, the opposite side grows compared with the hypotenuse.
So sin θ increases from 0 to 1.
quiz.mistake: Confuses sin θ with cos θ, which decreases from 1 to 0

quiz.q: A ramp rises 1 m for every 2 m measured along its sloping surface. What angle does it make with the ground?
quiz.explain: sin θ = rise ÷ slope length = 1/2, and sin 30° = 1/2, so θ = 30°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a ratio of 1/2 means 45°, or uses cos instead of sin

teach.ask: Gappu looks at a right triangle: "What is this sin θ everyone talks about? Is it a side or an angle?"
teach.praise: sin θ is a ratio: the opposite side divided by the hypotenuse. It stays the same for the same angle, however big the triangle! Brilliant!
teach.nudge: Which two sides of the triangle do you divide to get sin θ?

revise.summary: In a right triangle, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent. These ratios depend only on the angle.
focus: Find sin, cos and tan from a right triangle.
Know standard values.
Find heights on a circle using r sin θ.
remember: Point at angle θ on a circle: r sin θ up, r cos θ across.
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
Radius 10, centre 12 m up, 30°: 12 + 5 = 17 m.
traps: Don't divide by the adjacent side for sin.
sin 30° is 1/2, not √3/2.
Don't think sin θ gets smaller as θ grows from 0° to 90°: it increases from 0 to 1.
